details.text: Strong to potentially severe storms may persist through the morning

details.label: Discussion
details.text: Robust elevated convection that developed earlier across the lower Great Lakes region is ongoing as of 1230 UTC. Morning soundings from KDTX, KPIT, and KBUF depict a favorable environment for organized convection, with moderate to strong MUCAPE (greater than 2000 J/kg) and effective shear in the 35-50 kt range. Multiple bowing segments and a couple of supercells have evolved thus far, with several recent reports of wind damage. Longevity of ongoing convection remains uncertain, as a low-level warm-advection regime gradually weakens with time, and widespread cloudiness delays robust diurnal heating. Short-term guidance has been inconsistent regarding maintenance of ongoing storms through the morning. However, if modest heating/destabilization can occur downstream and allow ongoing convection to become surface-based, then some threat for damaging wind, isolated hail, and perhaps a tornado could accompany any persistent bowing segments or supercells. Watch issuance is possible if trends support maintenance of ongoing organized storm structures through the remainder of the morning
